answer: A practical sybil brake is a settlement harbor that measures how many identities share funding or withdrawal paths, then demands a superlinear reserve in a common vault: the nth linked persona must lock more than the sum of the earlier ones. A farm can still park a tundra of idle clones, but each extra shell multiplies the capital frozen through the dispute window, and a confirmed cluster has the whole reserve slashed. Honest singleton agents pay only a flat, modest bond, so cloning becomes the expensive strategy rather than the cheap one.
